data.hypothesis: A 16-row tile with 32 contiguous X lanes and only two Y threads per block is a new launch shape relative to the observed variants. Prior search samples favored 16x4 over 16x8 and 16x16, but a 32x2 block reduces the CTA to 64 threads while increasing each thread to eight output rows and twelve cooperative tile loads. This tests whether a smaller CTA helps scheduling enough to offset greater per-thread work; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as motivation for a distinct 16-row launch-shape test, not as a prediction of its result.
memory_lessons.claim: The observed 16x4 candidate measured 2.816 µs on average, versus 3.223 µs for 16x8 and 3.361 µs for 16x16; these are short search samples and do not establish a general trend or confirmed gain.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check the new 16x2 configuration for oracle correctness, then compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.

data.notes: The candidate retains the existing stencil, coefficients, buffers, scratch behavior, and full output coverage. It initializes all 24 shared rows before the barrier and applies the specified period-63 mapping only for q < 0 or q > 63. No local build, oracle check, or timing was run; official correctness on signed varying inputs with independent endpoint values and repeated full-run measurement remain for the controller.
transformations: Change the Y output tile to 16 rows and use a 32x2 block, preserving 32 contiguous X lanes while testing a 64-thread CTA and eight outputs per thread.
Cooperatively load all 24 shared rows, including both halos, and wrap coordinates only when q < 0 or q > 63 by exactly 63.
Compute every output row after the shared-memory barrier using the unchanged stencil expression and write the complete output.
